section: Educational Psychology · Ch2 — Piaget — Deep Practice 2
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A Class-9 student is asked: 'If all birds can fly, and a penguin is a bird, can a penguin fly?' The student recognises the logical validity of the argument even while knowing penguins cannot actually fly. This demonstrates:

options.option_text: Formal operational reasoning — separating logical form from real-world content

explanation: Recognising a syllogism's logical validity independent of its factual truth is a hallmark of formal operational thought (11+), which handles abstract, hypothetical propositions.

stem: A baby who searches for a toy only where it was PREVIOUSLY found, even after watching it being hidden in a NEW location, demonstrates the classic:
explanation: The A-not-B error is a well-documented sensorimotor-stage phenomenon where infants perseverate on the previous hiding location despite seeing the object moved — revealing incomplete object permanence.

subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A major criticism of Piaget's stage theory, supported by later research, is that:

options.option_text: Children often show some abilities earlier than Piaget's stage timelines suggested, when tasks are simplified
Piaget's stages have never been questioned by any researcher
Children show no individual variation in development at all
Culture and language have no bearing on cognitive development

explanation: Later researchers (e.g. using simplified tasks) found children demonstrate certain competencies earlier than Piaget's original timelines — his stage ages are now seen as somewhat conservative, though the general sequence largely holds.
